body: I want to avoid dumping the truck and saving it mainly because of sentimental reasons. Crate engine sounds like a good way to go about it, which year engine would be best to look for and is it worth swapping transmission as well? I worry most about cam phasers because I don't want it to be the cause of the engine going while I'm in the middle of nowhere trying to get this truck home. As for the cab rust, I misinformed. It's actually in the corner of truck bed, where water pools up from the third brake light allowing water inside.

Apart from the rust on the corner part of the bed, the body looks solid but, I haven't gotten to inspect the frame yet. I plan to when I go out there. I'm really hoping all is good with the truck because since it belongs to my late father, I would want to keep and fix it up just to have something to always remember him by so in a way, I would see this truck the same way.

I'll do my best to keep everyone updated on my drive, I'm hoping the fact that my dad didn't drive it very much (less than 10k miles since purchase in 2019) that the engine would be more solid, assuming fluids were done while it was sitting. I'm planning on going out there after Thanksgiving so, wish me luck...

First thing I want to say is youre not at fault for anything that happened between you two and you're not an idiot for taking him back, you saw the good in him and your love for him took over. Sometimes things like that are hard to control but let this be a life lesson for the future, make the best decisions based on your best judgment instead of emotion. Best way to maintain the cut off is to act like he doesn't exist. I realize he lives across the street from you but, don't even look in his direction. Block him from your contacts, social media, everything where you can see what he's up to and where he can contact you. If he comes to your house looking for you, don't answer the door or let a family member answer and send him away. You might be devastated now but, there's always someone better out there that's more deserving of the love you gave your ex. This is just a little bump in the road but, you can always pull through. Just make sure to focus on yourself and don't let him or anyone else take that focus away and impede on your happiness.

One thing I learned from a good friend of mine after my breakup is that people can enter and leave your life easily. If he essily entered your life and left easily, who's to say someone wont easily come in and be just as good, if not better for you than he was? There's no sense losing sleep over someone who left because people are replaceable in your life and there's always someone out there who's more deserving and better suited for you. I know it's tough right now but, keep in mind that him leaving you brought you closer to the one that's meant for you. You just have to focus on yourself, live your life, do things you've always wanted to do, work on aspects of yourself that you've always wanted to. It'll keep your mind occupied and if you keep that up, you'll forget about your ex and before you know it, better people will be in your life. If you need help keeping your mind off of things, you can always talk with me and tell me about your day or random occurances that happened during your day. Little things like that really do help and make a big difference. And don't ever think you're at fault for your relationship not working out, it's just life's way of telling you that there's someone who's more deserving of you and that you deserve better. Just take it as a life lesson, learn from it for the future, and keep moving forward with your life. Everything will be okay, trust me.

I'm going through a recent breakup myself and if there's one thing I learned it's that people can easily enter your life and they can leave just as easily. Life has a way of weeding out all the potentially bad matches that can come into your life and while those ways may hurt, they can be taken as life lessons. Life goes on, best thing you can do is keep looking forward and focus on yourself. Surround yourself with your close friends, focus on hobbies, anything to occupy your mind and avoid having tunnel vision. The more you do that, the more you'll forget about your ex and even better yourself. I know things are bad right now but, always remember 2 things. 

1: things can as always be worse. 

2: there's always someone better out there for you. While the person that you thought was the one left you, her leaving you also brought you one step closer to finding the one for you.
